title: Prospective Bidirectional Challenge
objective: Define a test that can FAIL CLEANLY after the release is frozen: a sealed, bidirectional (vector-to-place and place-to-vector) prospective challenge that freezes profile/software/scoring/tolerance and commits to a held-back actual before reveal, predicts a future anchor's pin/address with the frozen profile, records predicted-vs-actual against a pass/fail criterion, and grades SUCCESS / PARTIAL_SUCCESS / ALIAS_SET_SUCCESS / FAILURE.

claims.statement: A sealed challenge commits to the frozen profile, software version, scoring rule, tolerance, and a cryptographic hash of the held-back actual before reveal; run_challenge verifies the commitment (a swapped actual is refused), predicts the future anchor's pin (vector-to-place) or source vector (place-to-vector) with the frozen profile, and grades SUCCESS/PARTIAL_SUCCESS/ALIAS_SET_SUCCESS/FAILURE - the outcome CAN be a clean FAILURE.

negative_results: The synthetic held-back suite contains fixtures that FAIL: a vector-to-place prediction whose actual sits at the antipode, and a place-to-vector prediction whose held-back vector is wrong, both yield a clean FAILURE. The challenge is genuinely falsifiable, not rigged to pass.
Revealing an actual that differs from the sealed commitment is refused (ChallengeError) - the scoring, tolerance, and answer are frozen before reveal.
A passing challenge does not promote any predicted pin or route: it is a CALIBRATED_CANDIDATE at most, never a measured fact; proximity to any famous place is never rewarded.
privacy_check: CLEAN - synthetic/public future anchors, opaque challenge ids, and public coordinates only; no private path literals, no personal identity tokens, no raw private vectors or narrative
